主要内容: On April 20, 2016, Treasury Secretary Jacob J. Lew announced plans for the redesign of the U.S. $20, $10, and $5 notes. The new $20 bill will feature Harriet Tubman on its front, marking the first time a woman's portrait appears on U.S. currency in over a century. The reverse of the $10 note will depict the historic suffrage march ending at the Treasury Department, honoring leaders like Lucretia Mott and Susan B. Anthony. The $5 note will highlight events at the Lincoln Memorial and include figures such as Martin Luther King Jr. and Eleanor Roosevelt. The redesign aims to reflect the diversity of the nation and honor historical figures. The Bureau of Engraving and Printing will collaborate with the Federal Reserve to expedite the process, with the goal of releasing the new notes as quickly as possible while meeting security standards. The decision to feature Harriet Tubman on the new $20 was influenced by public feedback, particularly from children who viewed her as a role model. The new $10 will honor the women’s suffrage movement, including figures like Lucretia Mott and Susan B. Anthony, while the $5 will highlight events at the Lincoln Memorial, such as Marian Anderson’s 1939 performance and Martin Luther King Jr.’s 1963 speech. These redesigns aim to reflect the nation’s values and historical milestones.
